product_family: Bark is Suno's open-source text-to-audio generative model (transformer-based). It generates multilingual speech, music, sound effects, and non-verbal audio from text prompts. Available on GitHub under MIT license for commercial use. Note: This is an open-source research project, not a commercial SaaS service. Suno also offers a separate commercial music-generation service (Suno Studio, $30/mo Premier plan).

privacy.ai_training_note: Suno states: 'Voice recordings [are] retained for maximum three years following last user interaction' and 'Used to create voice models for audio generation features' and 'Processed to develop and enhance service models.' This means customer voice data is used to train/improve Suno's audio generation models. No opt-out mentioned for Bark specifically. For the open-source Bark model deployed locally or via third-party APIs, this does not apply: data handling depends on deployment context.

products.name: Bark (Open-Source Model)
products.data_scope: Self-hosted: user controls data. Via third-party APIs (Replicate, Hugging Face): depends on third-party provider's compliance. Via Suno's services: Suno processes voice/text per their privacy policy.
products.notes: MIT-licensed, free, open-source, commercial-use allowed. Generates speech, music, sound effects from text. Supports 13+ languages. ~12GB VRAM required for full model. No custom voice cloning. Outputs ~13 seconds max per generation. Development/research focus.

compare.pricing_model: Free (open-source). If using third-party APIs: Replicate charges per-second usage; Hugging Face depends on hosting model.
compare.data_residency: Depends on deployment: self-hosted = user's infrastructure; third-party API = API provider's infrastructure; Suno services = United States (primary)

flags: Nudge Security claims Suno holds SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, FedRamp, and CSA STAR Level 1 certifications. However, these certifications are not documented anywhere on Suno's official domain (privacy policy, terms of service, or dedicated security/compliance pages).
Suno does not maintain a publicly documented trust center or security certifications page. This is inconsistent with enterprise-grade security posture claims.
Terms of Service directs users to Privacy Policy for data handling details but does not independently document security commitments.
Bark repository does not disclose training data sources, composition, or methodology. Unclear whether copyrighted music or proprietary data was used.
Suno retains user voice recordings for up to 3 years to build voice models. Users may not opt out. This is a significant data use not clearly communicated in Bark's own documentation.

Nudge Security's security profile may reflect Suno's internal claims rather than independently verified certifications. The gap between claimed certs and documented certs on Suno's domain suggests either incomplete documentation or over-claiming.
As an open-source project, Bark itself has minimal formal security oversight. Security depends on code review by community and deployment context (local, third-party API, or Suno's services).
No SLA, no enterprise support tier, no formal security incident response policy documented.
Bark's README states 'Suno does not take responsibility for any output generated. Use at your own risk.' This limits vendor liability for misuse or generated content.
